newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy employers see rapid economic upturn unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Italy employers see rapid economic upturn unlikely.

text.p: A rapid recovery in Italy's economy seems unlikely and the risk of an upturn in inflation should not be under-rated, Giorgi Fossa, Chairman of the Italian employers' body Confindustria, said.

Fossa also told Confindustria's annual meeting that the fall in the country's inflation rate seen so far was partly due to stagnation of the economy and the effects of the lira's appreciation in 1996.

Fossa said the government in preparing its three-year economic plan document (DPEF) and the draft 1998 budget, "should not rely on a vigorous, spontaneous recovery in the economy which does not seem probable.
"And the risk of an upturn in inflation should not be under-rated," he added.

He noted that inflation had fallen rapidly to stand at nearly 30-year lows. "But this reduction is partly due to the stagnation of the economy and to the one-off effects of the lira's appreciation in 1996."
This fall in inflation had been made precarious due to rises in the cost of labour which were "more than double that of targeted inflation," he added.

Fossa said it was essential that the DPEF, due to go before the cabinet early next week, as well as Italy's convergence plan for early entry to the single European currency, should contain clear decisions concerning the budget for 1998.
